title.narrative: Linking Preparedness, survivor-led emergency response, well-being and long-term resilience Marsabit

description.narrative: Research from many different countries is revealing the extent to which crisis-affected communities are not only always the first-responders when disaster strikes, but often the most significant. Efforts are therefore being made to understand how the current norm of externally-led humanitarian interventions can be transformed into an approach that starts by maximising the impact of the survivor-led response. Not only can this be more responsive, quicker, more efficient and more holistic – it can also contribute to better psycho-social recovery and build and not undermine long-term community resilience. Furthermore, it also provides the chance to strengthen longer term resilience and help communities to start tackling root causes. The LPRR research revealed 6 key lessons which can inform our efforts to improve emergency response: (1) enable the community to co-run the response, (2) include psycho-social support, (3) remember the importance of community cohesion (togetherness) and good communication, (4) coordinate with other organisations and where possible work with the government or authorities (or advocate for rights) (5) identify and start to address the root causes, (6) include livelihoods and income generation immediately to empower, enable ‘power within’, give hope and avoid aid dependency. Under this proposed pilot project in Marsabit, we seek to build upon the gains of the recent drought emergency programme and assist local, drought-affected communities to improve their future resilience. It aims to do this through the following objectives; i. Giving micro-grants to active groups to improve the resilience of the drought-affected communities ii. Capacity building of the micro-grant groups in line with the identified gaps
